questions.html: Which of the following concurrency control protocol ensure both conflict serializability and free from deadlock?
questions.solution:

Both time stamp ordering and 2 phase locking protocol ensure conflict serializable but only time stamp ordering protocol provides freedom from deadlock.

options.html: B<sup>+</sup> tree index faster for range queries compared to B tree index.

If disk block allocated for B+ tree index and same size disk block allocated for B tree index. Then number of index blocks and cost of B+ tree index less than or equal to B tree index for given distinct keys.
If disk allocated for B+ tree index and same size disk block allocated for B tree index. Then B tree index access cost less than as equal to B+ tree index for given distinct keys.
If number of keys that can store in B tree and B+ tree index is same then cost of B tree index less than equal to cost of B+ tree index for.

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
If disk block allocated for B+ tree index and same size disk block is allocated for B tree index.
Then B tree index access cost is greater than B+ tree index for given distinct keys.
So option (c) is false.

questions.html: Consider a database system where transactions are executed concurrently. If transaction T1 holds an exclusive lock on resource R1 and requests a shared lock on resource R2, while transaction T2 holds a shared lock on resource R2 and requests an exclusive lock on resource R1, what will happen, transactions executed by using 2PL restriction?
questions.solution:
(a)
Deadlock occurs when transactions are waiting for locks held by each other, causing a circular dependency that prevents any transaction from progressing.

questions.html:
Consider the following relational schema:

Assume that, in the suppliers relation above, each supplier and each street within a city has unique name, and (sname, city) forms a candidate key No other functional dependencies are implied other than those implied by primary and candidate keys. Which one of the following is
TRUE about the above schema?

options.html: The schema is in 3NF but not in BCNF
The schema is in 2NF but not in 3NF

questions.solution:
(a)
The non-trivial FDs are
1. (sname, city) → street
2. sid → street
3. (sname, city) → sid
4. sid → name
5. sid → city
